meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English-derived company law per Companies Law Cap. 113) supplemented by civil-law statutory elements and directly applicable EU acquis with primacy.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cyprus–China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and Capital (effective 1990, amended 2018)
Cyprus–United Kingdom Convention on the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2017, effective 2018)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applicable to Cyprus)
EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (applicable to Cyprus)

Cyprus maintains a 60+ DTA network and 20+ investment protection treaties, including with the UAE, Singapore, Malta, Luxembourg and Russia (the Cyprus–Russia DTA of 1998 was terminated with effect from 31 December 2021).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Activities Law of 2007 (L. 188(I)/2007), as amended; Companies Law Cap. 113, ss. 113, 113A–113E as amended by L. 13(I)/2018 and L. 29(I)/2021 (central UBO register administered by the Department of Registrar of Companies); Regulation (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Regulation (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD), as transposed; Cyprus Bar Association AML Directives and ICPAC Anti-Money Laundering Regulations; Central Bank of Cyprus AML directions applying to the merchant-acquiring bank.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access – UBO statements are filed with the Department of Registrar of Companies; access is restricted to competent authorities, financial intelligence unit and obliged entities conducting customer due diligence; no public UBO access following CJEU judgment in C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 30 November 2022; nominee structures are regulated and require full disclosure of the underlying beneficial owner.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each UBO's valid passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Cyprus is a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the origin state is not party to the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the UBO's or corporate shareholder's good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed banking institution maintaining the relationship for at least 6 months

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association of any corporate shareholder (including a certified translation into Greek or English)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Cyprus incorporation agent and first directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each UBO/shareholder executing before a notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and signatories against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU autonomous sanctions (including EU Regulation 269/2014 as amended), Cyprus Ministry of Finance and Central Bank of Cyprus lists, OFAC SDN List (best-practice screening given USD settlement rails), Interpol notices and adverse-media sources; PEP status must be assessed per L. 188(I)/2007 Part III and any PEP identified requires senior-management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring; for a low-risk standard tea-lounge operation the screening protocol is streamlined but remains mandatory at onboarding and on an ongoing transaction-monitoring basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRC) – Online Name Reservation and e-Filing System (https://efiling.drc.mjpo.gov.cy), operated by the Ministry of Justice and Public Order of the Republic of Cyprus.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Greek and/or Latin (Roman) alphabets; where a Greek name is elected, a transliterated Latin version must be submitted and will be recorded in the certificate of incorporation. The corporate suffix must be 'Limited', 'Ltd' or the Greek abbreviation 'ΛΤΔ'. DRC practice requires transliteration to conform to standard Romanization rules, and any non-Greek/non-Latin word must be transliterated and accompanied by a certified translation. Foreign-language names are acceptable in transliterated form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: University / College / Institute (when implying state recognition)
Charity / Charitable (requires Minister of Interior approval)
Red Cross / Olympic / International Monetary Fund (protected emblems)
Holding / Group (requires evidence of the group structure or DRC discretionary approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are valid for six months from the DRC approval date with no statutory extension; if incorporation is not completed within that period a new name reservation must be filed. Upon rejection, the DRC issues a written refusal stating the conflicting or prohibited term; the applicant may, within 14 days of notification, submit a written request for reconsideration to the Registrar through the registered agent, attaching a curative name variant. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may file an annulment recourse before the Administrative Court of the Republic of Cyprus under Article 146 of the Constitution within 30 days of the adverse decision. The cost-effective alternative is to submit a fresh reservation using a distinctive generated element (e.g., geographic name + 'Specialty Tea Lounge' + registry sequence number).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted solely for the statutory registered-office requirement, provided the service is rendered by a licensed corporate services provider at a physical street address in Cyprus (a P.O. Box is prohibited). The specialty tea salon must occupy a licensed physical venue with municipal trading authorization, public-health registration, food-and-beverage premises certification and fire-safety compliance; a virtual office cannot satisfy operational substance, municipal licensing, card-acquirer due diligence or VAT registration substance expectations for a beverage-serving establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85–95% of newly licensed beverage-serving premises receive a physical municipal and health inspection within the first three months of operation, including pre-opening inspections by the municipal licensing authority and the Cyprus State General Laboratory/Health Services; thereafter unauthorized and unannounced hygiene, weights-and-measures and consumer-protection inspections are scheduled at least twice per year by municipal health inspectors and market surveillance authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act, Cap. 113, as amended, particularly sections 3, 4, 9, 10, 13, 17, 111 and 112
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property (RCIP), Nicosia, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form HE1 - Application for Registration of a Company, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private limited company; no escrow or deposit account is required. Shares may be issued at par, and partly paid shares are permitted if the Articles so provide.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers, having agreed to become members of the Company, do hereby adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed, and accept the allotment of shares set opposite each subscriber's name in the register of members. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at [address in Cyprus], and the Directors shall file the registered office particulars and any subsequent change with the Registrar of Companies. RESOLVED, that [Director A] and [Director B] be appointed as first Directors, and [Secretary] as Company Secretary, each being hereby authorized, jointly or singly, to execute onboarding filings, open bank accounts, and make all statutory declarations necessary for incorporation and commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property (RCIP) - Cyprus Business Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name clearance and reservation application through the RCIP portal. Verify that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to registered business names. Pay the prescribed reservation fee and obtain a name reservation certificate before filing constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Documentary proof of identity of each subscriber
Notarized power of attorney if filing through a lawyer or agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an administrative objection within 14 days or submit a revised name with the mandatory suffix 'Ltd'.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles with share capital, dividend, quorum and corporate governance provisions. The subscribers must sign in the presence of a notary or witness, and the signature pages must be initialled. Arrange for legalization or apostille if subscribers execute abroad.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association drafted in Greek or English with certified translation, if needed
Registered office consent from the property owner or tenant
Written consents to act as first directors and company secretary
Declaration of compliance with the Companies Act, Cap. 113
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the constitutional documents to correct drafting defects and re-execute before a notary; file a rectification application if the Registrar returns the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Dossier to Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCIP - Registration Section (physical counter or Cyprus Business Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form HE1 together with the signed Memorandum and Articles, statutory declarations, registered office address, officers' details, and payment of registration fee and capital duty. The Registrar reviews the documents for legal compliance; once satisfied, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Particulars of registered office (Form HE2 or equivalent)
Particulars of first directors and secretary (Form HE3 or equivalent)
Proof of payment of registration fee and capital duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Registrar's deficiency letter within 14 days; provide a supplementary explanatory statement or amend forms; re-submit through the portal and, if necessary, request priority review with the District Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate and Post-Incorporation Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation and verify the HE company number and date of legal personality. The directors must issue share certificates to subscribers, open the statutory registers, and record the share allotment in the register of members.
required_dossiers: Register of members, directors, and secretaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, apply for a corrected certified copy; rectify share certificates and re-date the register entries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Filings and Registered Office Disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCIP and Tax Department (Income Tax / VAT / Social Insurance Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the officers' appointments and registered office particulars in the public registry. Appoint a statutory auditor and make initial registration with the Tax Department, Social Insurance Services and VAT authorities if turnover crosses or is expected to cross the VAT threshold. Maintain the minute book and annual meeting calendar.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent or proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File late returns with an explanatory statement and pay administrative late fees; use the online correction facility to amend officer details.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licensing Committee of the local Municipality, acting under the Municipalities Law and the Licensing of Businesses and Premises Law
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food and Beverage Service Establishment Operating Licence - Specialty Tea Salon Lounge

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Low-risk registration / exemption - no full EIA Report required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Law No. 102(I)/2018
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer trade effluent consent limits; food hygiene standards under EC Regulation 852/2004; segregated waste collection and disposal under the Waste Law No. 185(I)/2011; noise and odour controls under occupational health and environmental regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Cyprus Fire Service; structural load clearance by an approved civil engineer; workplace occupational health and safety clearance from the Department of Labour Inspection; mandatory first-aid and fire-extinguisher equipment on premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Republic of Cyprus; electronic filing via TAXISnet portal (https://taxisnet.mof.gov.cy).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity conducting taxable activities in Cyprus must first obtain a certificate of incorporation or registration from the Department of Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property (DROCIP), then apply to the Tax Department for a Tax Identification Code (TIC), which serves as the VAT number where applicable. Non-established taxable persons supplying goods or services in Cyprus must register for VAT through a Cypriot tax representative unless an exception applies. The application must include corporate constitutive documents, identity and governance details, expected turnover, activity description, and registered address evidence. Registration for income tax is mandatory for companies managed and controlled in Cyprus or earning Cyprus-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope for non-resident entities (Cyprus-resident companies are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident companies are taxed on Cyprus-source income only; no pass-through eligibility for private limited companies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box election exists. Specific statutory elections available include group relief elections under the Income Tax Law, tonnage tax election for qualifying Cypriot-flag shipping activities, and the Intellectual Property (IP) Box regime election for qualifying intangible property. Hybrid mismatch provisions under EU ATAD apply, and no elective hybrid mismatch results are permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), governed by the Cyprus Value Added Tax Law of 2000 (Law 95(I)/2000), as amended.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration threshold is €15,600 in annual taxable turnover for established taxable persons supplying goods or services in Cyprus; non-established taxable persons are generally required to register from the first taxable supply in Cyprus, irrespective of turnover threshold. Separate thresholds apply for distance sales (€35,000) and intra-EU acquisitions (€20,000).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Cyprus does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime for domestic B2B invoices. Invoices must be issued in a secure format under VAT rules and submitted electronically through TAXISnet in VAT returns. Cross-border sales to EU customers are reported in the VIES listing. Cyprus is aligned with European e-invoicing standards for public procurement (PEPPOL) but has not yet implemented a general mandatory B2G/B2B e-invoicing clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods physically removed from Cyprus to a destination outside the European Union, to goods dispatched to another EU Member State under intra-Community supply rules, and to certain international services. The seller must be able to prove the goods left Cyprus within the statutory time limits and that title or export evidence is properly documented. Zero-rating for services applies where the place of supply is outside Cyprus or where the service qualifies as an export service under the VAT place-of-supply rules, subject to commercial and documentary evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / SAD)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank payment evidence
Proof of departure from Cyprus or arrival at destination outside the EU
Copy of the corresponding customs entry in the destination country where available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities examine export documentation in detail and may assess undeclared VAT with retrospective effect if zero-rating is not substantiated. Penalties include administrative fines, interest on unpaid tax, and, in cases of fraudulent or intentional evasion, criminal prosecution with possible imprisonment. Cyprus also implements EU mutual-assistance measures for cross-border VAT fraud, enabling clawback of input VAT previously recovered on zero-rated sales.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Κεντρική Τράπεζα της Κύπρου)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cyprus is a full member of the Economic and Monetary Union and the eurozone; the euro is the legal tender. There are no exchange control restrictions on capital or current account transactions. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, royalties and loan repayments are freely transferable abroad, subject only to standard banking compliance (customer due diligence, sanctions screening) and to appropriate corporate or tax withholding formalities where applicable. The target business of a specialty tea salon lounge (ISIC 5630) is a low-risk non-financial commercial activity, which does not require a CySEC licence; however, a Cyprus private limited company must demonstrate genuine economic substance and commercial purpose before tier-1 banks will maintain an unrestricted euro treasury account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Cyprus imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion requirements on export receipts. Exporters may retain and freely use foreign currency proceeds, and there is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio. Companies must only comply with customs and VAT declaration obligations related to export documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-High for EU/EEA licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions that passport into Cyprus under PSD2. Low for non-EU/EEA offshore digital EMIs, such as certain UK, UAE or Panama-domiciled platforms, which cannot provide a genuine Cyprus or EU IBAN account and are not recognized as primary treasury providers by the Central Bank of Cyprus or by local merchant acquirers. Offshore EMIs may be used only as auxiliary settlement channels but must never replace a regulated tier-1 domestic banking relationship for core working capital and tax disbursement purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors and natural-person beneficial owners is generally mandated for first-time opening of corporate accounts at tier-1 Cyprus banks. Remote or fully electronic onboarding is possible only where the bank has an approved e-KYC programme and the applicant is deemed low-risk and simply structured; however, in practice the compliance committee requires at least one physical or certified video-linked interview with the directors and the identification of all shareholders holding more than 5% before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive sales pattern and mixed tills typical of a high-end tea service lounge, presenting a potential layering or self-laundering red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS transaction reports, credit and debit card settlement statements, daily cash register reconciliation, VAT returns, corporate income tax filings, supplier contracts for tea and ceramics, UBO details, lease agreements, utility bills and a documented internal cash-management policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated private limited company with low EBITDA, passive minority shareholders and lack of clear commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Physical premises lease, photographs of the fitted tea salon, employee contracts and social insurance contributions, opening stock inventory, purchase invoices, menu and pricing lists, a projected three-year business plan, and Cyprus substance documentation aligned with tax authorities' internal circulars.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or sanctions-list screening against directors or beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed KYC forms, notarised passport copies, proof of residential address, source-of-funds declaration, source-of-wealth declaration, professional references, police clearance certificates and adverse media search reports showing nil results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers disproportionate to expected turnover, e.g. large inbound capital injections for a tea lounge.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, share issue certificates, board minutes authorising the contribution, official corporate registry filings, foreign inward investment declaration, and audited financial statements confirming the deployment of capital into leasehold improvements and inventory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be transferred via SWIFT MT103 over SEPA/TARGET2 rails using the beneficiary's IBAN and BIC. The remitter should reference the purpose code for direct investment or other investment/share capital, e.g. the Eurozone Balance of Payments 'share capital' category, together with a narrative of 'capital increase / paid-in share capital'. The receiving bank will verify the stated purpose, the source of funds and the corporate authorisation, and for amounts above EUR 50,000 it will require board resolutions and source-of-wealth documentation. Shareholder loans must use a separate BoP purpose code and be supported by a written loan agreement to avoid re-characterisation as equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to international suppliers primarily use SWIFT MT103 for open-account and documentary collection payments, with beneficiary country-specific correspondent bank instructions. For high-value or pre-shipment goods such as bulk loose-leaf tea imports and ceramic china, a commercial letter of credit is executed via SWIFT MT700/MT710/MT720. All outbound payments must comply with EU/EEA sanctions screening, confirm the underlying commercial invoice, and use an internationally recognised transaction purpose code. SEPA euro payments within the EEA can be processed as instant or normal SEPA payments; non-EEA payments must use the SWIFT network with a valid BIC and IBAN.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: European-style plain vanilla foreign exchange forwards (EUR/quoted currency)
FX swaps (principal and interest exchanged at initiation and at maturity)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies with limited external convertibility, used strictly for trade-hedging and never speculative
Cross-currency swaps permitted under EMIR trade reporting rules when entering into foreign-currency lease or financing agreements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form HE32) under s.153, Companies Law Cap. 113, together with the annexure of annual financial statements or the statutory abridged accounts for companies validly availing of the small-company audit exemption.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days immediately following the anniversary of incorporation (the statutory return date); anniversary-based and non-extendable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Graduated late-filing penalties apply for every completed month of delay under the statutory fee schedule (generally USD 54-270 / EUR 50-250); failure to file beyond 12 months exposes the company to s.327 administrative strike-off, and defaulting directors may be fined up to EUR 1,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cyprus applies a flat 12.5% corporate income tax rate with no local surcharges. The IP Box regime provides an effective 80% deduction on qualifying intangible profits. Dividends received from qualifying subsidiaries, profits from foreign permanent establishments, and gains on disposal of shares may be exempt. For a specialty tea salon with ceramic cultural services, no named statutory tax holiday applies; capital allowances are available on qualifying fixtures, tea machinery, and ceramic production assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the Cyprus Tax Department 'Tax For All' (TFA) electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the tax year-end (e.g., by 30 June for accounting periods ending on 31 December); provisional tax installments are due on 31 July and 31 December of the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, Cyprus HE registration number, registered address, and Tax Identification Number (TIN).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the registered HE77-series number; confirm the non-resident shareholders' details and any Cyprus tax representative appointments are current.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commencing and ending dates of the accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with the audited financial statements; for a non-resident-owned Cyprus Ltd, the standard calendar-year period is recommended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the commercial activity and applicable ISIC/NACE code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert ISIC 5630 and state 'Specialty tea salon and high-end loose-leaf tea service with ceramic cultural lounge activities'; use consistent wording across trade licences and VAT returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross revenue from tea sales, ceramic merchandise, lounge admission fees, tasting events, and ancillary services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Cyprus-source and foreign-source turnover allocable to the Cyprus operation; foreign-source income must be supported for any DTA relief claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to tea leaves, ceramic wares, food service inventory, packaging, and direct labour.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain stock counts and supplier invoices; costs must be incurred wholly and exclusively for the trade and supported by arm's length documentation for any import transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent, salaries, utilities, leasehold improvements, marketing, professional fees, and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only actual expenses are deductible; disallow private-use or non-trade elements; review connected-party service fees for strict arm's length compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax depreciation claimed on qualifying fixed assets, including ceramic kilns, tea brewing equipment, furniture, and leasehold improvements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate annual writing-down allowances using permissible Cyprus rates and retain asset purchase documentation for inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disallowable items, including fines, recognised income tax penalties, non-approved contributions, and capital expenditure incorrectly expensed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any related-party charges that fail the arm's length principle; document the basis for any transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available tax losses brought forward or carried back in accordance with the five-year carryforward limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the corporate ownership and business continuity conditions are satisfied; compute set-off against the current year's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable profit after all statutory add-backs, capital allowance claims, and loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base the calculation on the audited financial statements; if central management and control is asserted to be outside Cyprus, full evidence of management decisions and key meetings must be preserved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 12.5% on taxable income, less any provisional tax payments, credits, and tax withheld at source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not incur Cyprus Special Defence Contribution on dividends; no dividend withholding tax arises on a distribution to non-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission: administrative penalty of EUR 100 plus EUR 5 per day of delay, capped at EUR 200; additional tax of 10% of the assessed tax due if the return is filed late; statutory interest of 3.5% per annum on unpaid tax. For fraudulent or grossly negligent returns, penalties may rise to 100% of the evaded tax and criminal prosecution may follow.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Cyprus imposes no domestic withholding tax on dividends, so no DTA relief is required for ordinary dividend distributions. Where treaty relief is sought for interest or royalties, the beneficial owner must obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its residence jurisdiction, submit the Cyprus Tax Department's double tax relief application form together with the underlying contract and ownership evidence, and the paying Cypriot entity must retain the approved supporting file in the 'Tax For All' system before applying any reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory domestic withholding tax; 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive for qualifying associated EU companies; treaty rates may further reduce (commonly 0% under an applicable DTA). Interest: 0% domestic withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents; no DTA relief required; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive also eliminates withholding for qualifying associated EU enterprises.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where the aggregate value of controlled related-party transactions exceeds EUR 750,000 in a tax year. Master File: mandatory where the consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000 in the preceding financial year. A summary information form may also be required to be submitted with the IR4 return when the local file threshold is met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus does not administer formal zero-tax Economic Substance Regulations in the offshore/UAE mould. However, the central management and control doctrine, the OECD BEPS standards, and the EU ATAD general anti-abuse rule require genuine economic substance to preserve tax residence claims, benefit from the IP Box, support transfer pricing positions, and resist anti-avoidance challenges. A specialty tea salon with a physical outlet, engaged staff, inventory, and operational decision-making in Cyprus satisfies the requisite substance in practice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful falsification of books and records, understating cash receipts from tea lounge sales, overstating expenses, or maintaining a second undisclosed set of accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax equal to the tax evaded, statutory interest, and criminal penalties upon conviction: a fine not exceeding EUR 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to three years; in serious cases, confiscation orders may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly prepare or sign false returns are personally liable to prosecution; the corporate veil may be pierced for fraud, allowing civil recovery from personal assets; courts may impose travel bans and asset freezes during proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing or Non-Filing of IR4
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit the annual corporate income tax return within six months after the tax year-end.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of EUR 100 plus EUR 5 per day late, capped at EUR 200; additional tax of 10% on the assessed tax if the return is filed late; interest of 3.5% per annum on the unpaid amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Persistent non-filing can lead to summons against the directors and company secretary; if directors strip company assets to avoid payment, they may be held personally liable for unpaid tax and judgment debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain Local File/Master File, or submission of inaccurate documentation for related-party management fees, purchasing arrangements, or trademark licences above the EUR 750,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of EUR 500 per missing or incorrect TP document/obligation; possible arm's length re-adjustment by the Tax Department with interest and an additional penalty of up to 10% of the re-assessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve artificial profit-shifting arrangements or false TP declarations risk personal fines, disqualification, and criminal liability for tax evasion where the arrangement conceals taxable income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Legal Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the specialty tea salon as a letter-box facade with no real staff, premises, or inventory, or channelling fees to a zero-tax jurisdiction for fabricated services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to economic substance; denial of treaty benefits; application of CFC rules and general anti-abuse penalties of up to 100% of the contended tax; possible strike-off and dissolution under the Cyprus Companies Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign dormancy declarations while the company is active, or use the structure to defraud creditors, may face disqualification orders of up to five years, personal restitution orders, and travel restrictions applied by courts to secure tax collection.
